sources.title: Tournai et le Tournaisis 1188–1513
sources.institution: Service public de Wallonie / Institut Destrée / Segefa
sources.read: Full institutional text plus its period thematic map
sources.finding: Before 1513 Tournai French royal town and Tournaisis associated with Flanders suzerainty, different political-legal territories; clear boundary nuance.
sources.publication_rights: Map © original Atlas de la Wallonie, link only; not digitized

sources.title: Tournai et le Tournaisis sous influence anglaise (1513–1519)
sources.institution: Service public de Wallonie / Institut Destrée / Segefa
sources.read: Full institutional text and illustration; cross-checked academic MP controversy
sources.finding: Says English influence across Tournai city and Tournaisis, but mistakenly claims representation in Commons contrary to 1998 Davies. Its map is regional context not city wall or proof of all villages directly ruled.
sources.publication_rights: Map © Atlas de la Wallonie, link only; must not trace or mirror in repo

sources.title: Armand d'Herbomez review of Adolphe Hocquet, Tournai et l'occupation anglaise, 1513–1519
sources.institution: Bibliothèque de l'École des chartes / Persée
sources.read: Original published 1901 review accessible, original 1900/01 Hocquet monograph not read
sources.finding: Reviewer explicitly states Hocquet used then-local Tournai archives to outline how English administered both Tournai and Tournaisis from Sept 1513 to Oct 1518; latter endpoint is study interval/treaty, not necessarily actual garrison end Feb1519.

sources.title: Royal bailiff, lords and village communities: Tournaisis late 14th–16th centuries
sources.read: University bilingual detailed dissertation abstract; chapters and archival appendix not read
sources.finding: Since 1383 joint bailiwick Tournai–Tournaisis–Mortagne–Saint-Amand about 60 rural parishes, overlapping seigneurial courts, bailiff rights and commons; not full Tudor direct rule.
sources.publication_rights: Dissertation author retains copyright; link and paraphrase only

sources.title: Coutumes dans le bailliage de Tournai-Tournaisis au 16e siècle (2015, p.104)
sources.institution: UNamur Bibliothèque Universitaire Moretus Plantin / Bouquet Cartographique Wallon
sources.read: Item catalog and copyright notice; historical map content NOT downloaded, not digitized
sources.finding: A second specialist 16th-c thematic map of customary rights and bailiwick geography, not identified as exact 1513 English control.
sources.publication_rights: Copyright Protected, open access for reading, NO automatic permission to vectorize

sources.title: Carte du pays traditionnel du Tournaisis
sources.institution: Wikimedia Commons / cartographer FL00 80, based on Léon Vanderkindere (1902)
sources.read: Commons license and image overview, did not retrieve SVG content

sources.publication_rights: CC BY 4.0, reuse permitted with author FL00 80 attribution, license link and adaptation notice, but not traced in this release

sources.title: Tournaisis français — historical seigneurial holdings (secondary wiki lead)
sources.read: Summary of Saint-Amand abbey temporal powers and Mortagne lordship; citation by itself insufficient to assert same government 1513–1519
sources.finding: Saint-Amand abbey exercised high/low justice and Mortagne own seigneurial rights; later 'French Tournaisis' formations may be post-1668, do NOT backdate 1668 additions to 1513.

sources.title: GeoNames Tournai localities reference coordinates
sources.read: Indexed modern populated-place coordinates only; not historical survey
sources.finding: Verified modern centers of Tournai, Mont-Saint-Aubert, Templeuve, Blandain, Froyennes, Mourcourt, Havinnes, Ere, Esplechin, Antoing; former 1977 Tournai municipality cannot stand for 1513 bailliwick.
sources.publication_rights: GeoNames database CC BY attribution; coordinates reproduced as modern city nodes with source

sources.title: Lefranc's 1899 critical review of Armand d'Herbomez, Histoire des châtelains de Tournai de la maison de Mortagne
sources.institution: Bibliothèque de l'École des chartes / Persée
sources.read: Full accessible 1899 review page 519 (historic analysis of much earlier châtellenie, not direct 1513 register)
sources.finding: Older châtellenie / Tournaisis limits were Scheldt (Escaut), Scarpe, Elnon and Espierre river landmarks; Tournai town and suburbs EXCLUDED from historical châtellenie and parts of Saint-Amand/Mortagne lands similarly excluded. Distinguish early feudal geography from unified 1383 bailiwick and 1513 Tudor occupancy.
sources.publication_rights: paraphrase and link only; no derived historic map tracing

sources.title: Tournai-Tournaisis historical regional institutions diagram 1383–1793
sources.institution: Belgian science institution via Belnet ORFEO
sources.read: Search system extract from PDF only, original PDF returned 403; OCR/table may mislabel Henry VIII as Henry VII, verification pending
sources.finding: The court appeal chain for bailliage changes under English occupancy ca 1514–1519 (London Chancery appellate venue from 1517–19 in indexed extract), confirming distinct legal-administrative region; exact years and monarch in original figure unverified.
sources.publication_rights: citation only, do not reuse copyright diagram or its depiction

sources.title: Modern geocoded historical jurisdictional seats Saint-Amand-les-Eaux / Mortagne-du-Nord
sources.read: Modern settlement center coordinates sourced; not historic land-ownership map
sources.finding: Mortagne-du-Nord ~lat50.50368 lon3.45524, Saint-Amand-les-Eaux ~lat50.4492 lon3.4281 (separate mapcarta listing); historic seigneurial rights may differ from royal bailiwick.
sources.publication_rights: underlying OSM/GeoNames open data attribution applies

claims.label: Different institutions Tournai city vs Tournaisis
claims.what: Pre-1513 Wallonia summary reports French royal status of Tournai city and Flemish suzerainty over surrounding Tournaisis. English conquest of city in Sep 1513 must not imply whole pre-existing Flanders fiefs uniformly changed legal ownership.
claims.map: two semantic layers, town military-administrative vs Tournaisis possible bailiff influence

claims.label: British administration extended beyond city
claims.what: Hocquet (1900), in contemporary scholarly book review, studied English administration of Tournai and Tournaisis using archival municipality documents (Sep1513–Oct1518) and modern Wallonia atlas explicitly characterizes 1513–19 area as under English influence. This supports including region IN STUDY, not treating every parcel as identical direct administrative control.
claims.map: optional thin dashed lightly shaded Tournaisis historical influence mask, NEVER authoritative control polygon

claims.label: 60 villages ≠ 60 directly taxed/occupied English villages
claims.what: Mariage 2013 documents some 60 rural parishes within joint bailiwick Tournai-Tournaisis-Mortagne-Saint-Amand since 1383, with royal, lordship, village and ecclesiastical courts overlapping. Number is long-period administration description not 1513 town/village census nor compliance count.
claims.map: Do not automatically derive all village polygon or treat 60 as English direct-rule parishes

claims.label: Bishopric separate from urban bailiwick and Crown
claims.what: Davies 1998 notes contested Tournai episcopal jurisdictions among England, France, Habsburg Flanders; bishopric cannot be filled as English possession.

claims.label: October 1518 treaty vs Feb 1519 physical transfer
claims.what: Cession signed 1518-10-04. English local occupation persists to Feb 1519; 1519 year-end English control disappears. Review of 1900 monograph through Oct1518 does not override later physical departure.
claims.map: show 1513–1518 year-end influence on; 1519 year-end off

claims.label: No trace of modern atlas map without permission
claims.what: Wallonia Atlas modern copyrighted map 2013 and Mariage 2015 UNamur thematic map (Protected) can inform story but cannot automatically be copied, traced or digitised in source repository. CC BY 4.0 Commons traditional map may be reused with specific attribution but has different temporal/administrative scope.
claims.map: Generate original rough schematic from independent verified modern place centroid anchors; call it analytic distribution envelope, NOT digitised historical jurisdiction

claims.label: Rivers are historical old castellany guide, not the 1513 outer border
claims.what: Specialist 1899 review of Herbomez identifies old châtellenie Tournaisis by rivers Escaut/Scheldt, Scarpe, Elnon, Espierre, while expressly excluding city and banlieue plus parts of Mortagne/Saint-Amand lands. This relates to medieval feudal castellany which must not be equated automatically with 1383 later enlarged combined bailliage and actual English control after 1513.
claims.map: Future GIS may follow waterways only for earlier feudal entity with its own date; not use as 1513 direct crown boundaries.

claims.label: Institutional appellate chain changed after English occupation
claims.what: Belgian research publication indexed diagram proposes English Crown sovereign court for 1514-1515 and London Chancery 1517-1519 as appellate venue for Tournai Tournaisis bailiwick. Its PDF presently inaccessible and a monarch numeral potentially OCR-corrupted; corroboration with institution's primary court register required.
claims.map: Administrative reach strengthens need to map separate bailliwick layer; no numerical parish-level claim established.

regional_scope_note: This step advances from urban-only city-centre symbol to rough historic district orientation, without claiming full territory boundaries.
